title: Aggregate billing model for multi-candidate reranking: distinguish pre-rank work from final output billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers who use reranking/beam-search or multi-candidate generation pipelines are being charged in ways that are confusing and sometimes unfair. Our current metering treats each model pass that produces token output as independently billable, which leads to two concrete problems: (1) pre-rank candidate generation (many short candidates) can accumulate large token counts even though only one candidate is returned; (2) streaming + retry semantics can double-count candidate fragments when clients reconnect or when our fallback logic launches speculative candidate generators. Both behaviors surface as customer complaints and inaccurate quota enforcement.

Goal: Implement a robust, auditable metering semantics for multi-candidate pipelines that: (a) records pre-rank token work separately from the final-selected output; (b) supports configurable billing policies (charge-final-only, charge-final+preview, charge-every-pass) with clear defaults; (c) preserves accurate quota enforcement while avoiding ghost charges from retries/partial streams; (d) exposes detailed breakdowns in Console and invoices for transparency.

Scope: This ticket focuses on runtime-side metering changes and pipeline-level aggregation. Related UI/console surfaces and billing ingestion adjustments will be tracked separately but we will provide contract and sample payloads. Scope includes: tagging model-generated fragments with phase tags (pre_rank, reranker_score, final_output), adding idempotency/commit markers for candidate groups, and creating an aggregation step that computes billable tokens according to configured policy before writing final ledger entries.

Proposed design (high level):
- Metering events: extend the existing metering envelope to include "phase" and "candidate_group_id" and an explicit "commit" boolean for finalization. Pre-rank fragments get phase=pre_rank, final streamed selected candidate is phase=final_output.
- Candidate group idempotency: every rerank request receives a UUID (candidate_group_id) from the front-end or gateway. All produced fragments reference that id; the ledger aggregation step uses candidate_group_id + commit marker to dedupe retries.
- Two-pass ledger model (local aggregation): the edge-serving node emits provisional token tallies to an internal aggregation topic (kafka) labeled provisional:true. Only after a commit event is emitted for candidate_group_id does the aggregator translate provisional tallies into billable ledger entries (final:true). In case of abandonment (no commit within N seconds), provisional tallies age out and either are dropped or credited back depending on policy.
- Billing policies: implement three server-side policies configurable per-customer: "final_only" (default for most customers), "final_plus_preview" (final + X tokens of previews), "all_passes" (legacy behavior). The config is applied at aggregation time to convert provisional tallies into billable tokens.
- Quota enforcement: enforce provisional quota reservations when pre-rank tokens are produced, but only decrement committed quota at finalization; provide a provisional usage bucket in Console so customers see reserved vs committed usage. If provisional reservations exceed customer quota, we should block further pre-rank work or fall back to cheaper path (policy-configurable).
- Streaming edge cases: for streaming candidates we will require chunk-level idempotency tokens (sequence numbers + candidate_group_id). On reconnect, the gateway resubmits idempotency token; the aggregator ignores duplicate provisional tallies. Aborted streams without commit should not become permanent charges.

Trade-offs and risk:
- Revenue impact vs customer goodwill: final_only will reduce revenue for customers previously charged for every candidate. We mitigate by defaulting to final_only and offering opt-in for all_passes.
- Complexity and latency: adding provisional reservation and commit protocol increases complexity in edge serving and aggregator but should not materially increase customer-observed latency for the final_response path.
- Failure modes: commit never arrives (network partition). We define TTLs and automatic reconciliation jobs to either expire provisional reservations and optionally charge a conservative fallback (e.g., charge preview tokens).

Acceptance criteria:
- Metering envelope supports phase and candidate_group_id and commit marker in production runtime.
- Aggregator dedupes based on candidate_group_id and respects commit TTLs.
- Default billing policy set to final_only for new customers; legacy customers preserved.
- Console shows provisional vs committed token counts for reranker-heavy routes.
- Unit/integration tests covering streaming reconnect dedupe, aborted-stream TTL expiry, and policy conversion logic.

Implementation plan (rough):
1) Instrument runtime to attach candidate_group_id and phase tags (edge change).
2) Emit provisional tallies to internal topic along with idempotency keys. (ENG)
3) Implement aggregator conversion logic and ledger writer changes with policy switch. (ENG + Billing)
4) Quota reservation flow - provisional reservations and committed consumption. (Quota team)
5) Expose Console changes via an API contract (PM + Console).
6) Run canary on small set of customers, validate invoices and metrics.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout; opt-in customer config; migrate default for new customers. Monitor: charge-rate, refund requests, console mismatch alerts, and percent of provisional tallies expired.

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing how models produce candidates: it is purely a metering/aggregation and quota policy change. We will coordinate with Runtime and Billing to ensure compatibility with existing billing ingestion schema.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Investigation: ran sampling across top 50 reranker customers. Median pre_rank tokens per request = 420, final_output tokens = 80. There are outliers where pre_rank > 10k for LLM-based rerankers.

2026-03-04 - Design review w/ PM (Sara): PM requests explicit console surface for 'reserved' vs 'billed' tokens and a migration plan for enterprise customers. Follow-up: add API for retrieving provisional reservations per request.
2026-03-06 - Eng sync: decided to attach candidate_group_id at gateway level to simplify dedupe. Marco to prototype amended metering envelope schema. (Action: ENG prototype branch created)

2026-03-08 - Trade-off note: backend ledger change requires adding 'provisional' boolean to existing ledger rows. Billing team flagged downstream ETL impacts; agreed to add conversion mapping in billing-ingest.

2026-03-10 - Security review request: determine whether candidate_group_id could leak PII. Answer: candidate_group_id is a UUID; security advises hashing before logs. Added label 'security-review-needed' false for now but will follow up.
2026-03-11 - PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/12891 - prototype emits provisional tallies. Needs aggregator work before canary.
2026-03-12 - QA plan: add integration tests for streaming reconnect and commit TTL expiry. Partnering with QA to add synthetic reranker traffic harness.
